title: CoFE: Collaborative Feature Engineering via Semantically-Guided Exploration and Diagnostic-Driven Refinement

problem.claim: Feature engineering is a key bottleneck limiting tabular machine-learning performance.

gap.claim: Existing AutoFE methods may waste computation on semantically meaningless combinations, struggle with high-order interactions, and rely on coarse global metrics or insufficient structural context.

contributions.claim: CoFE is a two-phase framework coupling search-based exploration with LLM-driven reasoning.
Its exploration phase uses an LLM-constructed semantic feature schema to guide MCTS with semantic constraints and diverse complex candidate features.
Its refinement phase provides feature health reports containing sample-level and structural feedback for targeted LLM corrections.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 16 public tabular benchmarks reportedly show that CoFE outperforms state-of-the-art data-driven and LLM-based AutoFE methods on the majority of datasets.
The authors report favorable computational efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Feature engineering limits tabular machine-learning performance.
Existing data-driven and knowledge-driven AutoFE approaches have semantic, structural-context, interaction, and diagnostic-feedback limitations.
CoFE couples search-based exploration with LLM reasoning through semantic-schema-guided MCTS.
Feature health reports provide actionable sample-level and structural feedback for targeted corrections.
The authors report results across 16 public benchmarks with majority-dataset gains and favorable efficiency.

source_observation.claim: Semantic constraints and structural feedback are used at different stages of feature-engineering search and refinement.

interpretation.claim: Combining domain-aware search guidance with actionable diagnostics may reduce wasted exploration and improve iterative correction.

application.claim: Systems that generate complex candidates can pair semantic constraints during search with localized diagnostic feedback during refinement.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish effectiveness outside the reported tabular benchmarks or identify which datasets do not improve.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark identities, baseline implementations, or detailed evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not quantify performance gains or computational-efficiency results.
The abstract does not describe ablations, parameter settings, or reproducibility details.
